Slope and relative index of inequality from a survey design

Source: R/inequality_extras.R
survey_slope_index.Rd

Regression-based measures of socioeconomic inequality on the weighted fractional rank \(R\) (0 = poorest, 1 = richest; tie-aware as in survey_concentration_index()):

  • the slope index of inequality (SII), the slope of a linear regression of the outcome on \(R\): the absolute difference in the outcome between the richest and the poorest end of the distribution;

  • the relative index of inequality (RII), \(\exp(\beta)\) from a log-link quasi-Poisson regression on \(R\): the ratio of the outcome at the richest to the poorest end.

Both models are fitted with survey::svyglm(), giving design-based confidence intervals. Values of SII above 0 (RII above 1) mean higher levels among richer people.

Usage

survey_slope_index(design, outcome, wealth, conf.level = 0.95, by = NULL)

Arguments

design

A survey design object (survey or srvyr).

outcome

Unquoted name of the health variable.

wealth

Unquoted name of the ranking variable.

conf.level

Confidence level.

by

Optional character vector of grouping columns; ranks are computed within each group.

Value

A data frame with any by columns, n, SII, SII_lower, SII_upper, RII, RII_lower, RII_upper.

References

Mackenbach, J. P., & Kunst, A. E. (1997). Measuring the magnitude of socio-economic inequalities in health: An overview of available measures illustrated with two examples from Europe. Social Science & Medicine, 44(6), 757-771. doi:10.1016/S0277-9536(96)00073-1

Examples

set.seed(1)
df <- data.frame(wealth = rnorm(300), wt = runif(300, 0.5, 2))
df$sick <- rbinom(300, 1, plogis(-1 - 0.6 * df$wealth))
des <- survey::svydesign(ids = ~1, weights = ~wt, data = df)
survey_slope_index(des, sick, wealth)
#>     n        SII  SII_lower  SII_upper       RII RII_lower RII_upper
#> 1 300 -0.4911095 -0.6561048 -0.3261142 0.1473663 0.0752914 0.2884371
